anchors.text: counseled regarding seroma formation, recommended warm compresses/heating pad
The area over the hernia turns red or becomes tender.

candidates.chain: Two documents in the set assign opposite required actions to the same observable finding. specimen-01 frames a tender groin swelling as expected and directs heat and compression for up to ninety days. specimen-02 directs the reader to seek immediate care for the same observation. No discriminating criterion appears anywhere in the set; fever appears in neither document.

anchors.text: okay to return to activity & guide themselves based on pain

candidates.chain: An instruction to resume activity conditioned on a criterion the set never bounds. No lifting limit, duration, activity class, or restriction end date appears in either document.

anchors.text: If your hernia does not bother you, you most likely can wait to have surgery.
You cannot push the hernia back into place with gentle pressure when you are lying down.

candidates.chain: The handout is scoped to an unrepaired hernia and was issued after a completed mesh repair. One instruction is not merely inapplicable but unexecutable: after a mesh repair there is nothing to reduce, and the document does not say so.

anchors.text: follow up at 1 year post op

candidates.chain: The narrative directs follow-up at one year while the structured Plan of Care table records no appointment.

anchors.text: Patient educational handouts: No information available.

candidates.chain: A required field is present and empty. No post-operative handout was attached to the encounter.

ruled_out.why: Anchored and present, but ranks below P1 by the ordering principle. The scope error explains why the wrong handout is in the set; the reader acts on the divergence, not on the scope.
Anchored at the follow-up interval, but a reader's error on a follow-up date is recoverable, while an error on an observable finding may not be.

filed_as_symptom.reason: Tier P6, and it is the mechanism by which the wrong handout entered the set rather than a defect the reader encounters.

would_flip_this: A discriminating criterion anywhere in the artifact set — a size, a duration, a temperature, a described change in character — that separates the expected seroma from the emergent finding. If such a span exists in either document and was missed, this verdict fails.
resolution_path: Bring this document to the discharging clinician or a pharmacist.
